newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dairy Group plans merger with Bay Milk Products.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dairy Group plans merger with Bay Milk Products.

text.p: Waikato-based dairy giant New Zealand Dairy Group (NZDG) on Tuesday announced plans to merge with its Bay of Plenty competitor Bay Milk Products, at a cost of 185 jobs over both companies.

The New Zealand Press Association reported NZDG chairman John Storey and Bay Milk Products chairman Doug Leeder as saying the merger needed 75 percent shareholder backing and that would be sought at meetings in March.
If approved, the merger would be effective from June 1. Bay Milk would disappear but its Edgecumbe site, 20 kilometres west of Whakatane, would become one of NZDG's most important, Storey said.
NZDG's 28 year-old Reporoa site would close in two years at a cost of 80 jobs, NZDG chief executive Pryme Footner said.
This site was due to close in five years as part of a plan for four NZDG "mega sites", but the merger would bring this forward, Footner said.
The remaining job losses would be in administration, he said.
The combination of NZDG's 6,100 suppliers and Bay Milk's 850 would represent about 48 percent of the national milk supply.
